nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Solar photovoltaic systems|Photovoltaic cell efficiency_qna_000
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What should be considered when evaluating the energy efficiency of a solar photovoltaic system?
nodes.answer: Factors such as CO2 emission factors, SO2 emission reductions, and dust emission reductions need to be considered when evaluating the energy efficiency of a solar photovoltaic system.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Solar photovoltaic systems|Photovoltaic cell efficiency_qna_001
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What is one of the benefits of dye-sensitive solar cells (DSSCs) compared to silicon-based photovoltaic modules?
nodes.answer: Dye-sensitive solar cells are gaining popularity due to their cost-effectiveness and ease of fabrication, while silicon-based photovoltaic modules remain expensive despite their widespread use.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Solar photovoltaic systems|Photovoltaic cell efficiency_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What was the highest power conversion efficiency (PCE) achieved by the (MA-2 + N3) co-sensitization?
nodes.answer: The highest power conversion efficiency (PCE) achieved by the (MA-2 + N3) co-sensitization was 9.82%.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Solar photovoltaic systems|Photovoltaic cell efficiency_qna_003
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What is the conversion efficiency of N3?
nodes.answer: The conversion efficiency of N3 is 10.3%.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Solar photovoltaic systems|Photovoltaic cell efficiency_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What technique is considered promising for boosting the efficiency of Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells (DSSCs)?
nodes.answer: Co-sensitization is considered a promising technique for boosting the efficiency of DSSCs.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Solar photovoltaic systems|Photovoltaic cell efficiency_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How does co-sensitization enhance light absorption in DSSCs?
nodes.answer: Co-sensitization enhances light absorption by incorporating organic sensitizers that provide visible light alongside Ru (II) complexes that produce near-infrared light, achieving extensive spectrum sensitivity.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Solar photovoltaic systems|Photovoltaic cell efficiency_qna_006
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How does co-sensitization improve the performance of DSSCs?
nodes.answer: Co-sensitization improves DSSC performance by reducing dye aggregation, lowering charge recombination, and utilizing high molar extinction coefficients, which allows for better absorption of incoming photons.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Solar photovoltaic systems|Photovoltaic cell efficiency_qna_007
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the benefit of using smaller co-sensitizers in DSSCs?
nodes.answer: Smaller co-sensitizers are beneficial in DSSCs because they fill in the surface area left by larger sensitizers, optimizing overall light absorption and enhancing performance.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Solar photovoltaic systems|Photovoltaic cell efficiency_qna_008
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How does cyanoacrylic acid contribute to the performance of DSSCs?
nodes.answer: Cyanoacrylic acid establishes a robust ester connection with the TiO2 surface, facilitating electron injection towards the conduction band of TiO2, and also increases dye loading, resulting in higher power conversion efficiency (PCE).
